# Form & Field

Business: Form & Field, an independent architecture and interiors practice. This is a fictional sample brand with a complete, polished website.

## Visual direction
Chalk white, warm stone, black ink, restrained rust. Editorial Swiss grid, fine rules, architectural numbering, oversized but controlled serif headline, large cropped concrete photography. Compact typographic wordmark. Opening viewport: a slim header, two-column title and project note, followed by a panoramic photo with small caption. Avoid rounded SaaS cards.
Opening headline: “Spaces for the way we live.”
Do not reuse the starter's section order, blue gradients, mega-menu architecture, or giant grid of software services. Compose an intentional distinct design with a modest 4–6 section homepage, consistent inner pages, and a fully branded footer.

## Pages and navigation
Home: studio introduction, selected conceptual projects, three capabilities, process, invitation. About: philosophy, material choices, collaboration. Services: residential architecture, adaptive reuse, interior design. Work: three clearly labeled concept studies with approach and material notes. Journal: three useful notes on light, scale, and reuse. Contact: project inquiry form and consultation expectations. Service detail: residential architecture engagement.
All of these must be complete browseable pages with real sample copy. Navigation routes: Home /, About /about/, Services /services/, Work /work/, Journal /blog/, Contact /contact/, Privacy /privacy-policy/, and Service detail /services/featured/. Use these destinations consistently, relabeling the navigation naturally for this business. Use ordinary same-frame links so visitors can navigate the website inside an embedded preview. Every page must provide a route home and relevant next steps.

## Approved visual assets
Use only these prepared local files for imagery:
- assets/images/hero/editorial-hero.jpg — white concrete building
- assets/images/portfolio/editorial-detail.jpg — photo of beige concrete building
- assets/icons/mark-1.svg — Decorative interface mark
- assets/icons/mark-2.svg — Decorative interface mark
Use the approved photos at visually useful sizes and with deliberate crops. Supporting icon files can appear in process or footer details. Photography is illustrative stock, not work performed by this fictional brand; credit the photographers in a small image-credit section. Do not retain unrelated office photos, software terminology, or old brand copy in any page, form, unused component, documentation, or SVG.

## Interaction and accessibility
Use a minimal accessible mobile navigation with an operable hamburger, accurate expanded state, Escape close and visible keyboard focus. All pages must remain readable at 390px without horizontal overflow. Use a subtle CSS transition or intersection reveal with reduced-motion support; essential content must remain visible when JavaScript is disabled. Provide useful FAQ details, readable form labels, a friendly static-demo notice for submission controls, a skip link, and meaningful image alternatives. Forms must not falsely claim a message or payment was sent. No remote fonts, trackers, external runtime scripts, or dependency additions.
